claim: Patchline reports a reliability diagram and expected calibration error so that a stated confidence of eighty percent actually corresponds to being right about eighty percent of the time, letting a reviewer trust the abstain/act threshold. The worker bins predictions by confidence, computes the gap between mean predicted confidence and observed accuracy in each bin, and aggregates them into a sample-weighted expected calibration error. The gate proves a well-calibrated model's ECE stays under the acceptance threshold while a systematically overconfident model's ECE exceeds it.
